links.outcome: Triage category change under standardized lexical prompt perturbations
links.effect: 11.2% of repeated prompts changed triage category, with a maximum instability of 24.5%.
links.quote: Across standardized lexical perturbations applied to all 150 vignettes, 11.2% of repeated prompts changed triage category, with a maximum instability of 24.5%.

links.outcome: Subgroup undertriage rates (age, injury mechanism) hidden by aggregate accuracy
links.effect: Undertriage in geriatric scenarios 17.6% vs 5.2% in younger adults (P = .012); blunt 11.8% vs penetrating 4.1% (P = .045).
links.quote: Undertriage occurred disproportionately in geriatric scenarios (17.6% vs 5.2% in younger adults; P = .012) and was more frequent in blunt trauma than in penetrating trauma (11.8% vs 4.1%; P = .045).

links.outcome: Undertriage of major trauma (missed escalation) and simulated delay
links.effect: Simulated delay linked to undertriage affected 14.2% of major-trauma cases, mean theoretical delay 18.5 minutes; overall sensitivity 89.4%.
links.quote: Simulated delay linked to undertriage affected 14.2% of major-trauma cases and yielded a mean theoretical delay of 18.5 minutes.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance, subgroup undertriage, and prompt fragility on clinical trauma vignettes, but does not test an organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
